subject: Phased evidence handoff & staggered signature cadence (MSA / DPA / Order Form)
messages:
From: Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@crestlinehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + evidence handover windows (MSA/DPA/Order form)

Kimberly,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — team was impressed with the latency and the rollout options. Procurement and legal want to make sure we have a clear, phased MAP that ties evidence handovers to signature lanes (MSA -> DPA -> Order Form). A few asks from our side to avoid downstream blockers: 

- Can Redwood commit to a two-week evidence handover window for SOC2 artifacts and a separate 3-week window for data retention controls?
- We need the DPA redlines surfaced against the current template; Tom will attach the list of technical controls he needs verified.
- Would Redwood consider a staged signature approach so we can sign the MSA first, accept a pilot order form, and then finalize the full-volume orderform after acceptance testing?

Attached is our internal MAP spreadsheet — we marked hard dependencies and tentative gating dates. Please confirm if the sequencing below is realistic:

1) Security evidence & preliminary DPA review (2w)
2) Legal redline cycle + MSA signature (1w)
3) Pilot order form + acceptance testing (3w)
4) DPA finalization + full orderform signature (1w)

Can you loop in the legal lead and confirm the cadence?

Thanks,
Maggie Chen
Director, Procurement
Crestline Health

Attachments: Crestline_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.example
To: Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + evidence handover windows (MSA/DPA/Order form)

Hi Maggie — thanks for the clear outline and the MAP file. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Solutions) to confirm feasibility. Initial thoughts:

- Two-week window for SOC2 artifacts is reasonable if Crestline can provide the specific evidence list up-front. We can provide an evidence packet (signed attestations, control owners, sample logs) within that window.
- For data retention control validation we typically need configuration snapshots and a brief runbook; three weeks is conservative and should work.
- Staged signature (MSA -> pilot order form -> full order form) is something we do frequently for regulated customers. We recommend a stated pilot acceptance criterion in the MAP so legal and procurement have a deterministic gate.

Action items I propose (quick MAP iteration):
- Karthik: create a 1-page acceptance checklist for the pilot (SLA targets, sample PII flows, test queries).
- Laura: confirm any DPA clauses that must be agreed prior to the pilot (e.g., subprocessors, audit rights).
- Maggie/Tom: flag any high-priority controls that would block the pilot.

We also note that staggered signatures add bake time for procurement systems — if Crestline needs an internal approval for the pilot PO, call that out so we can align billing start dates.

I'll upload our draft MAP with versioning notes and proposed gating dates.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: kimberly_park@redwood.example, Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@crestlinehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@crestlinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP + evidence handover windows (MSA/DPA/Order form)

Maggie / Kim — quick legal view and redline ask.

Thanks for the MAP, Maggie. I'm comfortable with the phased approach provided we get clarity on three items before the pilot sign-off:

1) Minimum DPA clauses that cannot be deferred (audit rights; processor-subprocessor list updates). We can mark these as "MSA must include X before pilot" in the MAP to avoid rework.
2) Evidence scope: please annotate the MAP with examples of the artifacts (SOC2 type II summary, encryption-at-rest configuration, retention schedule table). The specificity speeds the handover.
3) Acceptance criteria for the pilot: Laura recommends 5 deterministic checks (connectivity, latency under p95 target, data isolation verification, logging/export, and an incident response runbook review).

I've attached preliminary redlines to the DPA and flagged the clauses I think will be contention points. If Crestline can accept our recommended fallback language on subprocessors and an audit cadence of 12 months, we can sign MSA and allow pilot to proceed under a conditional DPA agreement (final DPA to be signed within 30 days after pilot acceptance).

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v2.pdf

If you want, we can do a 30-min legal sync tomorrow to walk these tradeoffs.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@crestlinehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example, kimberly_park@redwood.example
Cc: Maggie Chen <maggie.chen@crestlinehealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + evidence handover windows (MSA/DPA/Order form)

Laura / Kim — thanks for the quick responses and helpful framing. Couple of clarifications from procurement/IT security: 

- We'll add artifact examples to the MAP today (SOC2 extract, key rotation logs, retention matrix).
- Conditional DPA sounds workable. Crestline requires that the pilot acceptance checklist be demonstrable (we prefer automated checks where feasible). Karthik, if you can surface the checklist and a short test harness (even Postman scripts) that would be ideal.
- Regarding billing: procurement prefers the pilot PO to kick billing at 50% of expected runrate while full orderform billing begins post-acceptance. We'll confirm internal approvals by next Wed.

Agree to a short legal sync — can you do 09:30 PT Mon 24 Aug? If so, we'll send a calendar invite and include our security engineer to review artifact formats.

Thanks,
Tom Alvarez
Procurement Lead, Crestline Health
